answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to post a bond that is slashed when independent audits find it double-voting or breaking a protocol rule. The bond is attached to a scarce, costly-to-obtain resource, not merely a new account, so copying identities does not multiply voting power for free. Audits can sample actions and compare signed records; a haven for honest agents might use a vine of reviewers, with juniper as the test network. A sybil attacker must lock up more capital for influence and risks losing it when caught.
